attempts.label: DANDI:001350
attempts.paper_title: SRF transcriptionally regulates the oligodendrocyte cytoskeleton during CNS myelination
attempts.entry_title: SRF in oligodendrocytes: corpus callosum TEM and sequencing (Iram, Garcia et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: Mostly untested: the hypomyelination of SRF knockout mice could not be checked, because the paper's hand scoring is not deposited and the masks cover one of five control mice. The sequencing findings largely held. SRF binds CArG-rich sites near promoters, Srf and Actb fall in knockout cells, myelin genes are not SRF targets, and the knockout changes 156 and 263 genes in progenitors and oligodendrocytes, matching the paper's counts. The number of high-confidence peaks and of shared targets held only in part, as the paper does not say how peaks and motif matches were chosen. Optic nerve, staining, culture and single-nucleus findings could not be tested, because the data are missing or need an R pipeline that was unavailable.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Iram, Garcia et al. (2024) on dandiset 001350, which holds 8000x TEM images of the adult corpus callosum of 5 SRF-Flox and 5 SRF-cKO mice with manual segmentation masks for some images, and on the paper's ChIP-seq and bulk RNA-seq in GEO GSE241561. From the masks it measures percent myelinated axons, myelinated axon density, g-ratio, myelin thickness and axon diameter; the masks cover one SRF-Flox mouse, so the paper's per-mouse comparisons cannot be run. From GEO it tests the SRF peak counts, their position and CArG motifs, and the genes SRF knockout changes in cultured OPCs and oligodendrocytes.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Iram, Garcia et al. (2024) from dandiset 001350
The sequencing claims of Iram, Garcia et al. (2024), from GEO GSE241561

outcomes.notes: The claim's test is an unpaired t test on per-mouse values of 5 SRF-Flox and 5 SRF-cKO mice (Figure 2C to 2E legends; Methods, Data Analysis and Statistics). The raw images of all 10 mice are in the dandiset (1779 to 4535 um2 per mouse), but the paper's hand scoring is not, and the masks that stand in for it cover one SRF-Flox mouse: the per-mouse measurements the test needs are missing for four of the five SRF-Flox mice and one of the five SRF-cKO mice, so the test cannot be run as the claim states; Welch's test is undefined and Student's test would borrow the cKO variance for the Flox group. The values the masks give are shown in the notebook and below; they do not decide the outcome. sub-370 (Flox) has 26.3% of its 3,842 counted axons myelinated (26.3% to 28.2% over readings O2 and O4), below the expected 37 +/- 3.7%. The cKO mean over four mice is 14.3% (14.3% to 18.9%), below the expected 22 +/- 2.2%, and lower than the Flox mouse under all 8 combinations; Student p for one Flox mouse against the cKO mice is 0.13 to 0.20. With images as units (2 Flox, 8 cKO) Student p is 0.014 and 0.036, Welch p 0.12 and 0.19. Counting unmyelinated axons without the pixels also in a myelinated fibre changes no mouse's percent by more than 0.02 points.
deviations: The paper scored and measured axons by hand in Fiji; the dataset's segmentation masks (AxonDeepSeg pseudo-labels corrected by hand, made after the paper) stand in for that scoring (reading O1 of the claims file).

The masks cover 8 full images and 2 small regions, from one SRF-Flox mouse (sub-370) and four SRF-cKO mice (sub-372, sub-373C, sub-374, sub-375), where the paper used 5 mice per genotype; sub-373C has 15 um2.

GEO's SRF consensus peak file (GSE241559) holds 848 peaks, the paper's number; this is a count of the deposited file, not a re-analysis of the reads. No reading of the high-confidence set is adopted, so measured holds only the 848. The high-confidence count depends on the reading of 'consistently across replicates within the same group and not in the IgG control'. With IgG peaks left out, peaks in all replicates of a group (OPC 4 of 4 or OLG 3 of 3) number 204 or 206, in a majority (3 of 4, 2 of 3) 312 or 316, inside 329 +/- 32.9, and in at least two 404 or 409. A majority without the IgG filter gives 329, but the paper excludes peaks in the IgG control. The paper's Dataset S1 lists 800 peaks in three sheets (OPC high 389, Common 351, OL high 60); 799 of them are peaks present in at least one replicate of the group and in no IgG control, so it holds no set of 329 that would settle the reading. The 848 holds; the 329 holds under one of three replicate rules, and the most literal reading of 'consistently', all replicates, gives 204. Changed from reproduced (resting on the majority reading) after verification round 1. The question is asked of the authors (finding).
deviations: The paper does not say how many replicates make 'consistently', nor which IgG peaks are excluded. Every reading is shown; none is adopted, as the paper's text does not single one out and the paper's peak lists (Dataset S1) do not hold the 329 peaks.
Read from GEO's processed nf-core outputs, not re-derived from the reads; GEO files are not versioned, and the SHA-256 of each file is printed in the notebook.

outcomes.notes: 545 of 848 peaks (64.3%) are within 2 kb of a TSS by HOMER's annotation (the paper's tool), and 76.0% of the high-confidence peaks. In the -250 to +250 window around each peak centre, FIMO matches of the JASPAR SRF matrix MA0083.3 (p < 1e-4) are in 10.7% of peaks, against 5.2% of flank windows 3 kb away (odds 2.2, Fisher p < 0.0001) and 3.7% of shuffled peaks (p < 0.0001); in OPC peaks 8.9% against 5.2% (p = 0.0007), in OLG peaks 14.4% against 4.3%. The strict consensus CC(A/T)6GG gives 9.8% against 3.0% and 2.4%. The consensus with one mismatch is not enriched over all peaks (38.9% against 36.7%, p = 0.28) or OPC peaks (p = 1.0), only in OLG peaks (p = 0.014). Peak windows are GC-richer than flank windows (0.546 against 0.449); within GC quintiles the enrichment over flanks stays (Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio 2.14 for FIMO, 2.75 for the strict consensus), and the shuffled background keeps each peak's composition.
deviations: The paper found its motif with MEME-ChIP, whose motif discovery is not run; FIMO is run with the JASPAR SRF matrix in place of the motif MEME-ChIP reported. Assumed: the paper's 'SRF CArG consensus' is the SRF matrix or the strict CC(A/T)6GG box, both of which are enriched; the one-mismatch variant is this attempt's own looser reading, not one the paper names, and is not enriched over all peaks.
'Most' is read as more than half.

outcomes.notes: With FIMO matches of the SRF matrix and each cell type's peaks as the Methods define them (present in at least one replicate), 43 CArG target genes are shared between OPC and OLG, 49.4% of the 87 genes of either group, so 'roughly half' holds and the count is outside 60 +/- 6. Egr1, Egr2, Egr3, Fos, Junb, Srf, Actb, Actg1 and Vcl, named in the paper, are all shared; Arc has no OPC peak. With the paper's own peak lists by group (Dataset S1) FIMO gives 42 shared of 85. Over twelve readings (three motif readings, four peak sets) the shared count is 7 to 133, and one reading gives a count inside the tolerance (56): the consensus with one mismatch, a reading of this attempt's own, on the majority high-confidence peaks, which drops Fos, Junb, Srf and Vcl from the shared genes.
deviations: The paper used FIMO matches of the motifs MEME-ChIP found and does not say which motif or threshold; FIMO is run here with the JASPAR SRF matrix at its default p < 1e-4. Assumed: the Methods' per cell type consensus ('peaks present in at least one replicate of the respective cell type') is the peak set of Figure 3D, and FIMO's default threshold.
Genes are HOMER's nearest genes of the peaks, as annotated in GEO's file.

outcomes.notes: DESeq2 (pydeseq2, default settings) on the RSEM gene results of GSE241560, KO against Flox per stage. The paper's normalized counts (Datasets S2 and S3, one stage each) are the expected counts divided by DESeq2's normalization factors from tximport's average-length offsets, computed per stage; with those factors the normalized counts here equal the paper's in every sample (spread of the log ratio over genes 0.0 to four decimals, median ratio 1.0001 and 1.0023), where size factors alone leave a spread of 0.09 to 0.21. So the paper used offsets (reading d). With the offsets and the DESeq2 vignette's pre-filter (at least 10 counts over a stage's samples), 156 genes have padj < 0.05 in OPCs (82 up, 74 down) and 263 in oligodendrocytes (92 up, 171 down), inside 157 +/- 15.7 and 264 +/- 26.4. They share 145 and 238 genes with the paper's tables, which hold 154 and 261 (Jaccard 0.88 and 0.83); p-values rank alike (Spearman 0.9996 and 0.998) and baseMean ratios are 1.000. Without a filter the offsets give 133 (outside the tolerance) and 266. Other readings, in this run, give 160 and 264 (b, length-scaled counts), 118 and 293 (a, rounded expected counts) and 130 and 418 (c, one model of all 15 samples). The round-2 run gave 117 and 294 for (a) and 130 and 423 for (c) with the same code and packages; a fit repeated on one machine is identical, and 15 to 44 genes per reading have padj between 0.045 and 0.055, so the difference most likely comes from the processor.
deviations: pydeseq2, the Python port of DESeq2, is used, as R is not available here. pydeseq2 takes only per-sample size factors; srf_geo.deseq_offsets puts DESeq2's gene-by-sample normalization factors where DESeq2 uses them (normalized counts, per-gene fits, Wald test). Given pydeseq2's own size factors it reproduces plain pydeseq2 exactly (printed).

The paper's tables list 13481 and 14851 genes, against 21688 and 27261 with any count here, so genes were filtered before testing by a rule the paper does not state. Assumed: the DESeq2 vignette's pre-filter (sum of counts at least 10). The outcome rests on it: without a filter the OPC count, 133, is outside the tolerance.

outcomes.notes: Under the per-stage readings (a), (b) and (d), Srf and Actb are lower in KO with padj < 0.05 in OPCs and oligodendrocytes (reading d, the paper's offsets, log2FC Srf -5.24 and -1.47, Actb -0.40, padj 0.040, and -1.44, padj 0.00001). Under the joint model (c), Actb in OPCs has padj 0.51. Actb and Actg1 are the actin genes with a CArG peak (FIMO or one mismatch); at p < 0.05 Actb is lower in both stages and Actg1 in oligodendrocytes (reading d, log2FC -0.43, p 0.028), and neither is higher. The paper's own tables agree with the per-stage readings: Actb log2FC -0.34, padj 0.044 in OPCs and -1.33, padj 0.00001 in oligodendrocytes; Srf -5.09 and -1.36. Datasets S2 and S3 each hold the samples of one stage, and their normalized counts match per-stage factors.
deviations: Down-regulated is read as log2FC < 0 with padj < 0.05, the paper's threshold for differential expression; the claims file gives no criterion. The adopted values are those of fig4ab-rnaseq-degs (reading d); reading (c) does not find Actb in OPCs.

outcomes.notes: Needs RNAscope images of P16 to P18 cortex, which are not in the dandiset, and the paper names no other deposit for them.

None of Mbp, Plp1, Mog, Mag, Mobp, Cnp, Cldn11, Pmp22, Mal, Opalin and Myrf is the nearest gene of any of the 848 SRF peaks (739 distinct nearest genes), so none is a target under any reading of the peak set or the motif.
deviations: The paper does not list its 'myelin genes'. Assumed: the structural myelin genes above, with Opalin and Myrf; a target is a gene that is HOMER's nearest gene of an SRF peak, the paper's annotation.

outcomes.notes: Tested on the claims file as amended after a reader's answer (questions/001350.yaml). Of the 12 disassembly genes of Fig. S4E other than Cfl1, none has padj < 0.05 in oligodendrocytes, and none of the 11 or 12 tested in OPCs does, under every reading. Cfl1 is lower in KO oligodendrocytes (reading d, log2FC -0.78, p 0.0004, padj 0.032; padj 0.024 in a, 0.029 in b and 0.0017 in c), against p 0.007 printed on Fig. S4F and padj 0.038 in the paper's table, and unchanged in OPCs (log2FC -0.04, padj 0.89). Actb is lower in KO in both stages under readings (a), (b) and (d); under the joint model (c) it is not in OPCs (padj 0.51). The paper names no set of actin assembly genes. Of 26 standard ones (Arp2/3 subunits, WASP and WAVE, formins, profilins, Ena/VASP, Actb and Actg1), Actb is the only one with padj < 0.05, and Actb and Actg1 the only ones with an SRF peak; in oligodendrocytes one of the assembly genes changes and one of the 13 disassembly genes does. The disassembly part and actin itself hold; that SRF mainly regulates assembly genes holds only through actin. Changed from reproduced after verification round 1, when the assembly genes were tested.
deviations: The claims file gives no criterion. The disassembly genes are those of Fig. S4E, and a gene is changed when DESeq2 padj < 0.05, the paper's threshold for differential expression (Results, "157 differentially expressed genes ( P .adj < 0.05)"; Figure 4A legend). "Largely unchanged" is read as at most one of the 12 other genes changed in a stage; none is. Assumed: the paper lists no assembly gene set, so the standard nucleation and elongation factors (srf_geo.ASSEMBLY_GENES) are used, with actin.

Assumed: the per-stage DESeq2 model adopted in fig4ab-rnaseq-degs (reading d). The joint model of all 15 samples (reading c) does not find Actb lower in OPCs, so the "actin itself included" part rests on this choice in OPCs; the paper's Datasets S2 and S3 hold one stage each.

The paper's enrichment analysis used the GeneTrail 3 web service with BH adjustment and its defaults (SI Methods), which cannot be run in a locked environment. The DESeq2 results it would start from are computed in geo_sequencing_claims.ipynb.

The count matrices are in GEO (GSM7794023, GSM7794024), but the claim rests on the paper's R pipeline: SoupX, DoubletFinder, scTransform and Seurat 4.3 integration, clustering at resolution 0.3 with manual annotation of clusters 0 and 2, and MAST. R is not available here (printed in the notebook) and these packages cannot be installed in the entry's locked Python environment; a Python substitute would change the clusters and the test the counts of 63 and 213 depend on. GEO (GSE243678) holds, for each of the two pooled samples, Cell Ranger count matrices (raw, filtered and after SoupX) but no cluster labels or cell annotations (listed in the notebook).
Rests on the clusters and MAST results of the R pipeline (see fig6b-snrnaseq-degs) and on GSEA; not runnable here for the same reasons.
The ranking of top up-regulated genes in oligodendrocyte clusters 0 and 2 rests on the R pipeline and MAST (see fig6b-snrnaseq-degs); not runnable here.

findings.statement: The paper's hand scoring of the corpus callosum TEM (axons counted, diameters and myelin thickness) is not deposited. The dandiset holds the raw images of all 10 mice and segmentation masks made later for a segmentation project, which cover 8 full images and 2 small regions from 5 mice, only one of them SRF-Flox. The paper's per-mouse comparisons of Figure 2C to 2E and Fig. S3C and S3D cannot be repeated from the dandiset.

Only the adult corpus callosum TEM of the paper is in the dandiset. The optic nerve TEM (Fig. S2), immunostaining, RNAscope, RT-PCR and culture imaging are not, and the paper names no other deposit for them; 14 of its findings cannot be tested.
The archive's summary gives 16 samples, where samples.tsv lists 86 (one per image, including two crops), and lists no species; participants.tsv gives the species as 'mus muculus'.

The dataset does not say which images were segmented or why, nor how its images relate to the paper's stitched 8 x 8 montages; image sizes differ by mouse (1482 to 5712 pixels a side). The two regions of sub-373C are exact crops of its sample-0001 at the README's coordinates, read as (column, row).

The axon-and-myelin mask of sub-373C chunk-01 is stored as grey with alpha and codes axon as 254 and 255, where the other masks are single-channel with axon 255. In the cKO images up to 51,098 pixels (0.23% of an image) are in both the myelinated and the unmyelinated axon masks; in the Flox images none are.

The Results say SRF regulates actin assembly genes and not genes that regulate actin disassembly, citing Fig. S4E and S4F, without naming an exception; Fig. S4F shows Cfl1, a main disassembly gene, lower in SRF-KO oligodendrocytes (p 0.007), and GEO's counts agree (log2FC -0.78, padj 0.024).

Question for the authors: how were the 329 high-confidence SRF peaks selected? 'Consistently across replicates' gives 204 peaks when read as all replicates of a group, 312 as a majority and 404 as at least two (each without an IgG peak); a majority without the IgG filter gives 329. Dataset S1 lists 800 peaks by group, not the 329.

Question for the authors: which genes were kept before the DESeq2 tests of the bulk RNA-seq? The paper's normalized counts show tximport's length offsets, and its tables list 13481 and 14851 genes where 21688 and 27261 have counts. With the offsets, the DESeq2 vignette's pre-filter gives 156 and 263 differentially expressed genes and no filter 133 and 266.

Question for the authors: which motif and threshold defined the CArG-containing target genes of Figure 3D, and which peaks (per cell type consensus or high-confidence)? FIMO with the JASPAR SRF matrix on each cell type's peaks gives 43 shared genes, against 60 in the paper; other readings give 7 to 133.

Question for the authors: what is the unit of Figure 2D, and which genes are the 'myelin genes' found not to be SRF targets? The dataset's masks give 0.82 to 1.09 myelinated axons per um2 in the mice with whole images, about half of the values the claims file reads from the figure in that unit.
The Results give 157 and 264 differentially expressed genes (padj < 0.05) in OPCs and oligodendrocytes; the paper's own DESeq2 tables (Datasets S2 and S3) hold 154 and 261.

disagreements.reason: The 848 is just the row count of the deposited consensus BED (problem 10). The 329 depends on the reading: 312 and 316 with a majority of replicates (in tolerance), 204 to 206 with all replicates and 404 to 409 with at least 2 (both out). A majority without the IgG filter gives exactly 329, which is not in the reading table and conflicts with the paper's 'not in the IgG control', so the 329 rests on a definition the notebook cannot pin down (problem 7).

entries.name: 001350-iram-2024
entries.title: SRF in oligodendrocytes: corpus callosum TEM and sequencing (Iram, Garcia et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Iram, Garcia et al. (2024) on dandiset 001350, which holds 8000x TEM images of the adult corpus callosum of 5 SRF-Flox and 5 SRF-cKO mice with manual segmentation masks for some images, and on the paper's ChIP-seq and bulk RNA-seq in GEO GSE241561. From the masks it measures percent myelinated axons, myelinated axon density, g-ratio, myelin thickness and axon diameter; the masks cover one SRF-Flox mouse, so the paper's per-mouse comparisons cannot be run. From GEO it tests the SRF peak counts, their position and CArG motifs, and the genes SRF knockout changes in cultured OPCs and oligodendrocytes.
